name: G4M Betty (our own model)
about: Made by tools/battle-models (aircraft). Metres; x forward, y right, z up. A battle model: `part` says which part each point belongs to; `parts` are the parts (parent, pivot, axis of turning, way of sliding); `sockets` are named places for flash, smoke, fire and wake; `clips` move the parts. Turns: +t degrees about an axis carries p to p cos t + (axis x p) sin t + axis (axis . p)(1 - cos t), about the part's pivot. Paints: 0 upper, 1 upper2, 2 under, 3 nose, 4 boss, 5 glass, 6 frame, 7 steel, 8 tyre, 9 blade, 10 line, 11 soot, 12 engine, 13 leg, 14 bomb, 15 stain, 16 glare, 17 glint, 18 torpedo, 19 torn, 20 blur, 21 blur_tip, 22 blade_back, 23 blade_band, 24 inside, 25 leather, 26 skin, 27 suit, 28 vest, 29 goggles, 30 exhaust, 31 boot, 32 lamp_red, 33 lamp_green, 34 lamp_white, 35 gunmetal, 36 patch, 37 lens, 38 rivet, 39 rivet_under, 40 seam, 41 seam_under

fly.about: Under way: every airscrew a turning disc, and she rides the air a little. The game flies her; this only lives on top.

idle.about: Engines ticking over on the ground or the deck: the blades are seen going round.

stopped.about: Engines stopped: blades still, no disc. For a parked machine.

bank.port.about: Rolls into a turn and holds it, her ailerons over as she rolls and her elevators up as she pulls round (lay it over `fly`; play it backwards to roll out).

bank.starboard.about: Rolls into a turn and holds it, her ailerons over as she rolls and her elevators up as she pulls round (lay it over `fly`; play it backwards to roll out).

fire.turrets.about: Her gunners firing back: a flicker at each gunner's muzzle, each turret and gun working a little about its aim (the game trains a turret at its target with the part's own axis and limits; this lies on top).

watch.about: Her gunners keeping watch: every turret and gun sweeping slowly across its piece of sky (lay it over `fly`).

torpedo_away.about: Her torpedo leaves: it drops clear and is gone, and she lifts as its weight comes off (the game's own torpedo is spawned at `torpedo` and takes over).

load.torpedo.about: She carries her torpedo, half out of her belly, and flies with the doors of her bay off: her bombs and her doors are not there (lay it over everything else).

load.bombs.about: She carries her bombs for bombing from high up: her torpedo is not there.

bombs_away.about: Her bombs leave: the doors of her bay swing open, her bombs drop out of it and are gone (the game's falling bombs are spawned at `bombs` and take over).

doors.close.about: The doors of her bay swing shut on an empty bay.

hit.about: Struck: she staggers and a puff of smoke and scraps flies from her.

smoking.about: Damaged but flying: a thin grey stream from an engine.

fall_burn.about: Shot down burning: an engine alight, she drops a wing and goes down in a steepening dive, trailing fire and black smoke. The game carries her down; this is her attitude, her fire and her smoke. Play `bail_out` over it if her crew get out.

fall_spin.about: A wing shot off: the port wing breaks away at the root, she whirls down out of control, the wing fluttering down behind her. The game carries her down.

fall_explode.about: Blown up: a burst of fire amidships, both wings and the tail fly off and the pieces tumble away, burning. The game carries the wreck down and takes it away at the end.

bail_out.about: Her crew take to their parachutes: 5 leave one after another (the game spawns the Parachute model at each `chute` event).

tally.note: a slot is a place in the game's axes and the way the skin faces there (x, y, z, nx, ny, nz); fill each list in order (rules)

panel.note: the fixed line: kills above it, bombs below it, the panel's front edge at x `front` (her own metres); `middle` is the middle of its first block, where the light test reads the paint she wears (rules.finish): `under` is her paint there and `blend` how far her coat is into `upper2` there when that is `upper` (a mottle or a patch); `colour` and `finish` are that paint as she is built. A plain machine wears her owner's colours: mix those the same way and test that

rules.missions: One bomb for each mission flown: mission k in slot k-1, from the front of the top row aft, ten to a row, new rows below, fifty to a block and the second block aft of the first. None past 100.
rules.kills: One symbol for each aircraft her gunners shot down, in the slots above the line, ten to a row from the front, new rows upward. Group them by symbol (`victims` gives each victim nation's), the commonest first, ties by the symbol's name (A to Z). Kills with no nation recorded join the first group (KILL-PLANE when none is recorded). A nation in `own` paints its own symbol for every kill, as one group. Lay out: each group starts a row of its own, from that row's first slot; a group of more than ten fills whole rows and runs on into its next row, so a nation is never split between rows. While that takes more than three rows: from the end, join the last two neighbouring rows that fit together in one row of ten (one slot empty between groups); when no two neighbours fit, take away every row after the third and put their groups back singly, the largest first, each whole into the row it leaves the least room in (ties: the later row), one slot empty before it. A group that fits nowhere is not shown. tallies.kill_rows is the reference. The slots keep a third of a symbol's width between symbols: never draw them closer.
rules.hand: `hand` is the painter's hand for this airframe, one entry a slot: [lean in degrees, size, along, up]. Draw the mark upright on her side (the decal's up along her skin toward the sky, its right toward her tail), turned by lean (positive turns it anticlockwise as seen from outside her), scaled by size, and moved along metres toward her tail and up metres up her skin. Missions first, then kills. For another aircraft of the same type start at another slot: entry (k + 37 * seat) mod the list's length.

tins.rule: each row of bombs takes one tin; the newest row the first tin, the row before it the second, and so on round (start one later for each seat)

fade.rule: the newest mark at full strength, each older one a step paler: the first bomb at 0.67 of the newest's contrast (draw it at that opacity over the skin). Kills fade within each row, the front one oldest, but only to 0.85, so a red disc never reads pink nor a blue disc lose its blue. Never so far that a mark drops out of the count

finish.rule: the finish under the panel, not the aircraft's name: test the paint she wears at `panel.middle` (the middle of the panel's first block), camouflage, mottle and her owner's colours included: her paint `panel.under` there, and when that is `upper`, mixed `panel.blend` of the way to her `upper2` (with a plain machine's owner's colours for each where the owner gives them). Light when its lightness L* is at least this. `panel.colour` and `panel.finish` are the answer for her own paint. Use the decals' dark or light set to match, for the whole panel

rules.damage: The battle marks the tally as it marks the skin: draw soot, oil and bullet holes over it.
rules.decals: tally/tally-sheet.png and tally-sheet.json: each tag's picture for a dark and a light finish. A bomb's is white with its black edge (on a light finish): multiply it by its row's tin.
